title: Common Denominators of Fire Behavior on Tragedy Fires

nodes.text: Identify common denominators of fire behavior on tragedy fires

evidence.source_text: Common Denominators of Fire Behavior on Tragedy Fires

nodes.text: Recognize fires often occur on relatively small fires or deceptively quiet areas of large fires

evidence.source_text: 1. On relatively small fires or deceptively quiet areas of large fires.

nodes.text: Recognize fires often occur in relatively light fuels, such as grass, herbaceous fuels, and light brush

evidence.source_text: 2. In relatively light fuels, such as grass, herbaceous fuels, and light brush.

nodes.text: Be aware of unexpected shifts in wind direction or wind speed

evidence.source_text: 3. When there is an unexpected shift in wind direction or in wind speed.

nodes.text: Monitor fire response to topographic conditions and uphill runs

evidence.source_text: 4. When fire responds to topographic conditions and runs uphill.

nodes.text: Be cautious during critical burn period between 1400 and 1700

evidence.source_text: 5. During critical burn period between 1400 and 1700.

nodes.text: Consider alignment of topography and wind during critical burning period as a trigger point to reevaluate tactics

evidence.source_text: Alignment of topography and wind during the critical burning period should be considered a trigger point to reevaluate tactics.

nodes.text: Understand blowup to burnover conditions can occur in less than 60 minutes, as little as 5 minutes

evidence.source_text: Blowup to burnover conditions generally occur in less than 60 minutes and can be as little as 5 minutes.

nodes.text: Consider a tactical pause around 1400 to reevaluate situation awareness of topography, weather, and fuel

evidence.source_text: A tactical pause may be prudent around 1400 for reevaluating your situation awareness of topography, weather, and fuel.

nodes.text: Complete evaluation of common denominators and adjust tactics as necessary
